summary: ansible-core 2.19 standardizes error handling so warnings and errors include operational context and the data involved, and task errors appear consistently in task results; message text is not stable.
questions: Why do Ansible 12 error messages look more verbose or repetitive?
Can I parse Ansible error message text in automation?
Where do task errors appear in the result in ansible-core 2.19?

answer_card.title: Contextual warnings and errors
answer_card.answer_md:
Internal error handling changed in ansible-core 2.19. Most warnings and errors now include the **operational context** (what was happening) and the **data involved**. Errors during task execution are more consistently put in the task result, with full details for callbacks and a short message in the result's `msg` field.

Some messages may look redundant for now. Error message contents are **not stable**, so avoid automation that depends on their exact text.
